prompt: This is an art-direction redesign for Yorimichi, a stylised Japanese autumn exploration game made in Unreal. Image 1 is a real, unretouched screenshot of the game as it is now. Repaint THE SAME VIEW from the same camera, keeping the layout, street grid, terrain, building positions, sea and sky composition, but redesigned to the standard of a polished commercial stylised game (think Ghibli-inspired, hand-crafted, cosy, dense and lived-in): textured materials with soft hand-painted detail instead of flat untextured colour, coherent warm autumn palette, gentle afternoon sunlight. It must stay a believable real-time game frame built from meshes, textures and foliage, not a loose illustration. No text, no UI, no watermark. The railway station and its forecourt from above. Today: a bare pale plaza and empty mint field around the station, with a row of sparse trees. Redesign: a lively station square with textured stone paving, a bus and taxi stop, bicycle parking racks full of bikes, a kiosk, vending machines, planters and street trees, a small shop row and houses around the square, railway tracks and platforms with fences behind the station, utility poles, signage boards. Dense and lived-in, like a small Japanese seaside town station.
